The card uses NASA POWER, GPM IMERG, SMAP and MERRA-2 data for a 20-year climate picture, and it also reports how far to trust the advice. details:
SoilVerity (Terra Loop), is a web-based decision-support tool for the Field Shift challenge. It helps farmers choose better crop rotations using local conditions and NASA Earth-observation data.

A farmer enters their location, last two crops, water source, Soil Health Card values, and priorities. The tool then generates a Rotation Card comparing three or more possible crop rotations. It uses 20 years of climate information from NASA POWER, GPM IMERG, SMAP, and MERRA-2 to make the recommendation more grounded.

Its key differentiator is transparent trust scoring rather than a black-box AI recommendation:

  • Source agreement: Labels advice as Solid, Mixed, or Fragile based on agreement across NASA datasets.
  • Switch or stay verdict: Tells the farmer whether changing the current rotation is advisable.
  • Missing-input alert: Identifies the one piece of information that would most change the recommendation.

Overall, SoilVerity aims to make climate-aware crop-rotation planning practical, explainable, and accessible for farmers.
dataRefs: SMAP L4 Global 3-hourly 9 km Surface and Root Zone Soil Moisture (SPL4SMGP)
